papers.title: Benchmarking Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials for Temperature-Dependent Elasticity of Binary and High-Entropy Refractory Carbides
papers.shortTitle: Which universal potentials capture high-temperature stiffness of carbides?
papers.authors: Miroslav Lebeda, Jan Drahokoupil, Šimon Svoboda & Petr Vlčák
papers.versions: Nine uMLIPs benchmarked; MACE-MH-1 and DPA4-Mini named in the abstract
papers.systems: Refractory carbides: five binary and two high-entropy carbides between 300 and 1200 K; elastic constants and bulk, shear and Young’s moduli.
papers.result: Nine uMLIPs are benchmarked against consistent AIMD data using stress–strain molecular dynamics, which samples thermal motion and anharmonicity. MACE-MH-1 has the lowest overall error (5.7%); MACE-MH-1 and DPA4-Mini reproduce thermal softening best. All models tend to underestimate stiffness, C12 shows the largest model-dependent errors, and group-V carbides (especially TaC) are hardest; high-entropy carbides are described as accurately as binary ones.
papers.note: Own work (IMPLANT Team). Only two of the nine models are named in the abstract; add the rest to the model tags if wanted.

papers.title: Thermal conductivity predictions with foundation atomistic models
papers.shortTitle: Can foundation models predict heat transport and thermal expansion?
papers.versions: Foundation models compared in the paper; fine-tuning protocols included
papers.systems: Thermal conductivity and thermal expansion of 103 solids with diverse compositions and structures.
papers.result: Using the Wigner formulation of heat transport and the Grüneisen approach to thermal expansion, the authors test foundation models on anharmonic, experimentally observable thermomechanical properties. They provide standards and fine-tuning protocols needed for first-principles accuracy, applied to 103 solids.
papers.note: Model list from the paper text.

papers.title: NEP89: universal neuroevolution potential for inorganic and organic materials across 89 elements
papers.shortTitle: A neuroevolution potential across 89 elements at near-empirical speed
papers.versions: NEP89 (GPUMD)
papers.systems: Inorganic and organic materials across 89 elements: alloys, solid electrolytes, water, salt dissolution, combustion and protein–ligand dynamics.
papers.result: NEP89 is a foundation model based on the neuroevolution potential, trained on a compact dataset curated by descriptor-space subsampling. It is reported to match representative foundation models while being three to four orders of magnitude faster, enabling million-atom simulations; fine-tuning is supported.
papers.note: Implemented in GPUMD.

papers.title: The Open Materials 2024 (OMat24) inorganic materials dataset and models
papers.shortTitle: 110 million DFT calculations for inorganic materials
papers.versions: EquiformerV2 models trained on OMat24, MPtraj and Alexandria
papers.systems: Inorganic materials with broad structural and compositional diversity, including non-equilibrium structures.
papers.result: Meta FAIR releases OMat24, an open dataset of over 110 million DFT calculations, with pretrained EquiformerV2 models. The models led the Matbench Discovery leaderboard, with stability F1 above 0.9 and formation-energy accuracy of about 20 meV/atom. The paper studies model size, denoising objectives and fine-tuning.
papers.note: First posted on arXiv 16 Oct 2024 as “Open Materials 2024 (OMat24) Inorganic Materials Dataset and Models”. The dataset behind several later Meta models, including UMA.

papers.title: Performance of Meta’s Universal Model for Atoms across the Conformational and Configurational Space of Diverse Transition-Metal Catalysts
papers.shortTitle: How reliable is UMA for catalyst conformers?
papers.authors: Adarsh V. Kalikadien & Evgeny A. Pidko
papers.venue: The Journal of Physical Chemistry A
papers.versions: UMA; see source for evaluated checkpoint
papers.systems: Homogeneous transition-metal catalyst complexes: their conformers and configurations, including near-degenerate conformers. Not surface reactions.
papers.result: UMA rapidly screens transition-metal complexes, but ranking reliability depends on coordination and flexibility. Near-degenerate conformers need particular care; aggregate errors can hide unreliable ligand-level rankings.
papers.note: Homogeneous transition-metal complexes; this is not a surface-reaction benchmark.

papers.title: Foundation models for atomistic simulation of chemistry and materials
papers.shortTitle: Where foundation interatomic potentials are heading
papers.versions: Survey of MLIP foundation models
papers.systems: Chemistry and materials broadly; not tied to one material class.
papers.result: This Perspective reviews machine-learned interatomic potentials and argues that scaling diverse datasets and expressive architectures should yield foundation models that are more efficient, transferable, robust out of distribution and easy to fine-tune.
papers.note: A review / perspective article.

papers.title: Platonic representation of foundation machine learning interatomic potentials
papers.shortTitle: Do different foundation models learn a shared geometry?
papers.versions: MACE-MP-0 variants; MACE-omat; Seven-omat; Orb-v3 variants
papers.systems: Not a single material class: compares the learned representations of MACE, SevenNet and Orb foundation models, with phonon-related failure examples.
papers.result: An atomic-anchor transformation aligns the latent spaces of independently trained MLIPs. The authors connect distortions in the aligned geometry with examples of physical prediction failures.
papers.note: The filter date is the verified first-posted date. The journal version appeared in 2026; its exact online publication date is not recorded in this seed.

papers.title: Revealing interstitial energetics in Ti-23Nb-0.7Ta-2Zr gum metal base alloy via universal machine learning interatomic potentials
papers.shortTitle: Mapping C, N, O and H interstitials in a disordered Ti–Nb alloy
papers.authors: Miroslav Lebeda, Jan Drahokoupil, Veronika Mazáčová & Petr Vlčák
papers.venue: Journal of Materials Research and Technology
papers.versions: MACE-MATPES-PBE-0, Orb-v3 and SevenNet-0
papers.systems: Ti-23Nb-0.7Ta-2Zr (at.%) gum metal base alloy (bcc): C, N, O and H interstitials in octahedral and tetrahedral sites.
papers.result: Three uMLIPs map interstitial energetics in a disordered gum-metal alloy orders of magnitude faster than DFT, giving broad energy distributions (~1–3 eV). MACE-MATPES-PBE-0 and Orb-v3 reproduce the expected bcc site preferences (C, N, O octahedral; H tetrahedral), whereas SevenNet-0 wrongly favours octahedral H, confirmed by DFT. Ti-rich environments stabilise interstitials; nearby Nb destabilises them.
papers.note: Own work (IMPLANT Team). Filter date is first arXiv posting; the journal record gives only the issue month (March 2026).

papers.title: A foundation model for atomistic materials chemistry
papers.shortTitle: The MACE-MP-0 foundation-model reference
papers.versions: MACE-MP-0 series; published study primarily MACE-MP-0b3
papers.systems: Broad atomistic materials chemistry: bulk inorganic materials, surfaces, catalysis, metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) and phonons.
papers.result: MACE-MP-0 demonstrates broad transfer from a materials-focused training set to diverse atomistic systems, with stable dynamics and examples of both qualitative and quantitative agreement.
papers.note: The first preprint was submitted on 29 December 2023. Filtering uses the journal’s online publication date, not the preprint identifier year.

papers.title: FastCSP: Accelerated Molecular Crystal Structure Prediction with Universal Model for Atoms
papers.shortTitle: Molecular crystal structure prediction with UMA alone
papers.versions: UMA, no system-specific fine-tuning
papers.systems: Molecular crystals and polymorphs for pharmaceuticals and organic electronics: 28 semi-rigid and 10 flexible molecules, 74 experimental polymorphs.
papers.result: FastCSP is an open-source crystal structure prediction workflow driven entirely by UMA, with no DFT or fine-tuning. It recovers all 74 known polymorphs, ranked within 9 kJ/mol of the global minimum, and reproduces dispersion-inclusive DFT closely.
papers.note: Open-source workflow released with the paper.

papers.title: Universal machine learning interatomic potentials poised to supplant DFT in modeling general defects in metals and random alloys
papers.shortTitle: Universal potentials for defects in metals and high-entropy alloys
papers.versions: Several pretrained universal models; EquiformerV2 performs best
papers.systems: Metals and alloys: grain boundaries and defects in pure metals, high-entropy alloys, hydrogen–alloy and solute–defect interactions; tungsten case study.
papers.result: Pretrained universal potentials are tested on a wide range of defects in metals and alloys. The latest EquiformerV2 models reach DFT-level accuracy (energies below 5 meV/atom, forces below 100 meV/Å RMSE), outperforming specialised MTP and ACE potentials. A tungsten case study shows pure-W data alone is insufficient.
papers.note: Only EquiformerV2 is named in the abstract; see the paper for the other models.

papers.title: Fine-tuning foundation models of materials interatomic potentials with frozen transfer learning
papers.shortTitle: Fine-tuning MACE-MP with partially frozen layers
papers.versions: MACE-MP foundation models, fine-tuned with frozen layers
papers.systems: Reactive chemistry at surfaces, and stability and elastic properties of ternary alloys.
papers.result: Fine-tuning foundation models with partially frozen weights reaches chemical accuracy using 10–20% of the data (hundreds of points), comparable to models trained from scratch on thousands. A cheaper surrogate model can then be trained on the fine-tuned potential.
papers.note: Model family from the paper text.

papers.title: UMA: A Family of Universal Models for Atoms
papers.shortTitle: One model family across materials, molecules and catalysts
papers.versions: UMA small and medium model family
papers.systems: Inorganic materials, molecules and catalyst systems, trained across combined materials, molecular and catalysis datasets.
papers.result: UMA combines training across materials, molecular and catalyst datasets with a mixture-of-linear-experts architecture to improve the balance between inference speed, accuracy and model capacity.
papers.note: The filter date is first posting. The report was revised on 4 March 2026; this entry is not a claim about the latest released checkpoint.

papers.title: A framework to evaluate machine learning crystal stability predictions
papers.shortTitle: The standard leaderboard for crystal-stability prediction
papers.versions: Models on the initial leaderboard; the online leaderboard is updated continuously
papers.systems: Inorganic crystals: thermodynamic stability (energy above the convex hull) in high-throughput materials discovery.
papers.result: Matbench Discovery evaluates ML energy models as pre-filters for finding stable inorganic crystals, with a Python package and an online leaderboard. Universal interatomic potentials performed best (F1 0.57–0.82, up to 6× discovery acceleration). Accurate regressors can still give many false positives near the 0 eV/atom hull boundary.
papers.note: Known as Matbench Discovery; first posted on arXiv 28 Aug 2023. The online leaderboard (matbench-discovery.materialsproject.org) is updated continuously. A publisher correction exists: doi.org/10.1038/s42256-025-01117-4.

papers.title: Universal machine learning interatomic potentials are ready for phonons
papers.shortTitle: Which universal potentials get phonons right?
papers.versions: Universal models available at the time of the study
papers.systems: Harmonic phonon properties of about 10,000 inorganic crystals from ab initio phonon calculations.
papers.result: The study benchmarks universal potentials on harmonic phonon properties using around 10,000 ab initio phonon calculations. Some models predict phonons accurately, while others show large errors despite good energies and forces near equilibrium.
papers.note: Model list from the paper text; check the paper for exact checkpoints.

papers.title: MACE-OFF: Short-Range Transferable Machine Learning Force Fields for Organic Molecules
papers.shortTitle: A transferable MACE force field for organic molecules
papers.venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society
papers.versions: MACE-OFF (small, medium, large)
papers.systems: Organic molecules: gas and condensed phases, molecular crystals and liquids, peptides and a solvated small protein.
papers.result: MACE-OFF is a series of short-range transferable ML force fields for organic molecules trained on high-level quantum-mechanical data. It reproduces torsion scans, molecular crystal and liquid properties including nuclear quantum effects, free-energy surfaces in solvent and peptide folding dynamics.
papers.note: An organic-molecule foundation model rather than a periodic-table-wide one.

papers.title: The Open Molecules 2025 (OMol25) Dataset, Evaluations, and Models
papers.shortTitle: 100 million high-level DFT calculations for molecules
papers.versions: Baseline models released with the dataset
papers.systems: Molecular chemistry: small molecules, biomolecules, metal complexes and electrolytes; 83 elements, charge/spin states, solvation and systems up to 350 atoms.
papers.result: OMol25 contains more than 100 million DFT calculations at the ωB97M-V/def2-TZVPD level, covering ~83 million unique molecular systems with explicit solvation, variable charge and spin, conformers and reactive structures. Baseline models and evaluations are provided.
papers.note: Baseline model families from the paper text; check the paper for exact checkpoints.

papers.title: Machine learned potential for high-throughput phonon calculations of metal—organic frameworks
papers.shortTitle: Fine-tuning MACE for high-throughput MOF phonons
papers.versions: MACE-MP-0 and fine-tuned MACE-MP-MOF0
papers.systems: Metal–organic frameworks: phonons, thermal expansion and bulk moduli (127 training MOFs).
papers.result: MACE-MP-0 predicts MOF structures well but struggles with phonons. A fine-tuned model, MACE-MP-MOF0, trained on 127 diverse MOFs, corrects imaginary modes and improves phonon densities of states, enabling quasi-harmonic thermal expansion and bulk moduli consistent with DFT and experiment.
papers.note: A worked example of targeted fine-tuning for a difficult materials class.

papers.title: Orb-v3: atomistic simulation at scale
papers.shortTitle: Do universal potentials need equivariance and conservative forces?
papers.versions: Orb-v3 model family (conservative and direct-force variants)
papers.systems: General atomistic simulation of materials, including properties that need higher-order derivatives of the energy (e.g. phonons).
papers.result: Orb-v3 maps the trade-off between accuracy, speed and memory, with more than 10× lower latency and 8× lower memory at near state-of-the-art accuracy. The authors report that non-equivariant, non-conservative architectures can still model physical properties accurately, including those that require higher-order derivatives.
papers.note: Useful for choosing between Orb-v3 variants for large or long simulations.

papers.title: Learning Smooth and Expressive Interatomic Potentials for Physical Property Prediction
papers.shortTitle: Why energy conservation in MD predicts real-property accuracy
papers.versions: eSEN models (ICML 2025)
papers.systems: Inorganic materials: stability prediction, thermal conductivity and phonon calculations.
papers.result: The authors propose testing potentials on whether they conserve energy in molecular dynamics; models that pass show better correlation between test error and downstream property accuracy. Design choices that cause failures are identified, leading to the eSEN architecture with state-of-the-art results on stability, thermal-conductivity and phonon tasks.
papers.note: Published at ICML 2025 (proceedings without a DOI); arXiv version linked.

papers.title: Universal Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials are Ready for Solid Ion Conductors
papers.shortTitle: Six universal potentials tested on solid electrolytes
papers.versions: MatterSim, MACE, SevenNet, CHGNet, M3GNet and Orb (ORBFF)
papers.systems: Solid-state electrolytes for Li-ion batteries, including Li₃YCl₆ and Li₆PS₅Cl: energies, elastic moduli and Li-ion diffusion.
papers.result: Six universal potentials are compared on energies, forces, thermodynamics, elastic moduli and Li-ion diffusion in solid electrolytes. MatterSim performs best on nearly all metrics. Case studies show how anion disorder and Na/Li arrangement affect ionic conductivity.
papers.note: Preprint version.

papers.title: Systematic softening in universal machine learning interatomic potentials
papers.shortTitle: When a universal potential makes the energy landscape too soft
papers.versions: MACE-MP-0, CHGNet and M3GNet evaluated in the study
papers.systems: Off-equilibrium properties of solids: surfaces, defects, phonons and ion-migration barriers.
papers.result: Three early universal potentials systematically underestimate energies and forces across several off-equilibrium tasks. Local fine-tuning can reduce the bias caused by an overly soft potential-energy surface.
papers.note: Single-configuration corrections are local demonstrations, not a universal one-point fix. Classified here as an application benchmark, with implications for model development.

papers.title: Application of pretrained universal machine-learning interatomic potential for physicochemical simulation of liquid electrolytes in Li-ion batteries
papers.shortTitle: Using SevenNet-0 to simulate Li-ion battery electrolytes
papers.versions: SevenNet-0, plus a fine-tuned version
papers.systems: Liquid electrolytes for Li-ion batteries: 20 solvents; solvation, density and ion transport.
papers.result: SevenNet-0, trained mainly on inorganic compounds, predicts solvation, density and ion transport of liquid electrolytes in good agreement with experiment and ab initio data, with systematic density errors. Fine-tuning corrects these at much lower cost than building a bespoke model.
papers.note: Filter date is first arXiv posting; the journal record lists only the publication year.

papers.title: DPA-2: a large atomic model as a multi-task learner
papers.shortTitle: A multi-task pretrained “large atomic model”
papers.versions: DPA-2 (DeePMD-kit)
papers.systems: A wide range of chemical and materials systems pretrained jointly, for fine-tuning and distillation to downstream tasks.
papers.result: DPA-2 is proposed as a prototype “large atomic model” pretrained on diverse chemical and materials data with a multi-task approach. It generalizes better across downstream tasks than single-task pretraining with fine-tuning, and is designed to be fine-tuned and distilled.
papers.note: Large author team (43); part of the DeePMD ecosystem.

papers.title: Orb: A Fast, Scalable Neural Network Potential
papers.shortTitle: A fast universal potential built with diffusion pretraining
papers.versions: Orb (v1/v2 family described in the report)
papers.systems: Inorganic materials: geometry optimization, Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics, including out-of-distribution materials.
papers.result: Orb is a family of universal potentials reported to be 3–6 times faster than existing universal models and stable in simulation on out-of-distribution materials. On release it reduced error by 31% on Matbench Discovery. The report explores diffusion pretraining for materials foundation models.
papers.note: Superseded for most uses by Orb-v3 (also in this collection).

papers.title: Performance Assessment of Universal Machine Learning Interatomic Potentials: Challenges and Directions for Materials’ Surfaces
papers.shortTitle: Bulk training does not guarantee reliable surface energies
papers.authors: Bruno Focassio, Luis Paulo Mezzina Freitas & Gabriel R. Schleder
papers.versions: MACE, CHGNet and M3GNet as evaluated in the 2024 study
papers.systems: Surface energies of inorganic materials (slabs), compared with the mostly bulk training data.
papers.result: The study finds substantial surface-energy errors for three broadly pretrained MLIPs and relates these shortcomings to the mismatch between bulk-dominated training data and surface environments.
papers.note: Published online 11 Jul 2024 (issue dated 5 Mar 2025); first posted on arXiv 7 Mar 2024.

papers.title: Scalable Parallel Algorithm for Graph Neural Network Interatomic Potentials in Molecular Dynamics Simulations
papers.shortTitle: Making equivariant GNN potentials run in parallel MD
papers.venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation
papers.versions: SevenNet (NequIP architecture); pretrained SevenNet-0 on Materials Project data
papers.systems: Large-scale molecular dynamics of inorganic materials, demonstrated on SiO₂ and amorphous Si₃N₄ with more than 100,000 atoms.
papers.result: The paper introduces a spatial-decomposition parallelization scheme for message-passing equivariant potentials and the SevenNet package interfaced with LAMMPS. It reaches over 80% weak-scaling efficiency on 32 GPUs; strong scaling drops when GPUs are under-used. A Materials Project pretrained model, SevenNet-0, is released.
papers.note: Relevant if you need multi-GPU MD with a universal model.

papers.title: MatterSim: A Deep Learning Atomistic Model Across Elements, Temperatures and Pressures
papers.shortTitle: A foundation potential built for temperature and pressure
papers.versions: MatterSim model described in arXiv:2405.04967
papers.systems: Bulk inorganic materials across elements, temperatures and pressures: structures, vibrational properties and finite-temperature thermodynamics.
papers.result: MatterSim uses active learning to sample a broad range of atomic configurations and demonstrates prediction of structures, vibrational properties and finite-temperature thermodynamics.
papers.note: This entry describes the linked 2024 report. Its label does not assert that no later peer-reviewed version exists.

papers.title: CHGNet as a pretrained universal neural network potential for charge-informed atomistic modelling
papers.shortTitle: The charge-informed foundation for inorganic materials
papers.versions: Original CHGNet model
papers.systems: Inorganic solids with charge or magnetic-moment effects, such as mixed-valence and battery materials: phase behaviour and ion transport.
papers.result: CHGNet incorporates magnetic-moment supervision into pretraining and demonstrates charge-informed modelling of phase behaviour and ion transport in inorganic solids.
papers.note: Included as a foundational reference, not as a new model release.

papers.title: A universal graph deep learning interatomic potential for the periodic table
papers.shortTitle: A three-body graph network trained on Materials Project relaxations
papers.versions: M3GNet universal IAP trained on Materials Project relaxation trajectories
papers.systems: Inorganic crystals across the periodic table: structure relaxation, molecular dynamics and stability screening of hypothetical crystals.
papers.result: M3GNet adds three-body interactions to a graph neural network and is trained on ten years of Materials Project structural relaxations. Screening 31 million hypothetical crystals flagged about 1.8 million as potentially stable; of the 2,000 lowest-energy candidates, 1,578 were confirmed stable with DFT.
papers.note: One of the first broadly used universal potentials; a common baseline in later benchmarks.
